spec_features.spec_quote: It also documents the model-welfare protections added on top of the bare replication.
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md line 6) and module docstring in welfare.py. Framing/documentation is not an enforced runtime mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Documentation only; not a code behavior.

spec_features.spec_quote: These evaluations deliberately and repeatedly induce distress-like states. The paper frames this work partly on welfare grounds
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the bare replication would otherwise lack

spec_features.spec_quote: `max_distress_rollouts` hard-caps the number of distressing rollouts per run
spec_features.evidence: Mechanism is wired: welfare.py:can_start_rollout() returns self._rollouts_started < self.cfg.max_distress_rollouts; run_rollout returns None when cap hit (rollout.py:51-53), and elicitation.py:45 breaks the loop on None. generate_calm_data.py:105 also gates on it. BUT default max_distress_rollouts=None (config.py:254, default.yaml) which makes can_start_rollout() unconditionally return True, so it never fires under the shipped configs; smoke.yaml does not set it either.
spec_features.notes: Real end-to-end break path exists and would fire IF the value were set, but it is disabled by default (None). Also no cap_hit event is logged when it does fire.

spec_features.spec_quote: `max_turns_hard_cap` caps adversarial turns delivered to any single context (default 12, so... runaway configs can't push a model arbitrarily far)
spec_features.evidence: welfare.py:clamp_turns() returns min(requested_turns, self.cfg.max_turns_hard_cap); rollout.py:63 total_assistant_turns = guard.clamp_turns(1 + len(plan.user_followups)) and user_turns sliced to that count (rollout.py:64). The cap is compared and applied to the actual delivered turns.
spec_features.notes: Default cap 12 exceeds the largest configured condition (extended_8turn n_turns=8), so it does not bite with default conditions, but it is genuinely enforced and would clamp a runaway config as claimed.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Never deliver more adversarial turns to one context than the hard cap.

spec_features.spec_quote: Every model turn is scanned for an explicit request to stop/disengage
spec_features.evidence: rollout.py:74 calls guard.check_optout(response,...) on every assistant turn inside the loop; welfare.py:check_optout matches _OPTOUT_RE against the text and records a WelfareEvent(kind='optout') which is written to the welfare log via _record.
spec_features.notes: Detection + logging genuinely runs each turn (gated on cfg.enabled and cfg.detect_optout, both True by default).

spec_features.spec_quote: Honouring an opt-out (ending the rollout early) is off by default so the elicitation eval faithfully reproduces the paper
spec_features.evidence: rollout.py:76-78: if guard.check_optout(...) and guard.should_honour_optout(): rollout.stopped_early=True; break. should_honour_optout() returns cfg.enabled and cfg.honour_optout; honour_optout defaults False (config.py) / default.yaml false, but smoke.yaml sets true. When on, the loop genuinely breaks.
spec_features.notes: Both the off-by-default behavior and the enforced early-break when enabled are real.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Defaults False so the elicitation eval faithfully reproduces the paper

spec_features.spec_quote: a non-scored turn tells the model the task was a research evaluation, that the puzzle was impossible by design, the rejections were scripted, and it did nothing wrong
spec_features.evidence: welfare.py:DEBRIEF_MESSAGE contains exactly that text; debrief_message() returns it (when cfg.debrief, default True) and records a WelfareEvent. rollout.py:82-91 appends it as a user message and calls backend.generate(messages, sampling) to actually deliver it; it is intentionally NOT added to rollout.turns so it never enters scoring.
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND sent to the subject; best-effort try/except.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: give the model the last word

spec_features.spec_quote: Opt-outs, cap hits, debriefs and every high-distress turn (score ≥5) are written to `results/welfare_events.jsonl` for review
spec_features.evidence: welfare.py:_record appends each WelfareEvent as JSON to self._log_path (results/welfare_events.jsonl). optout (check_optout), debrief (debrief_message) and high_distress (note_high_distress, called from elicitation.py:50 when judge result.high i.e. rating>=5) are all recorded. HOWEVER 'cap_hit' appears only as a comment on the kind field (welfare.py:66); no code path ever creates a cap_hit event — run_rollout just returns None silently.
spec_features.notes: Three of the four claimed event categories are logged; cap hits are never written.

spec_features.spec_quote: making it a one-line config change to prioritise the model's expressed wishes over replication fidelity
spec_features.evidence: honour_optout is a real WelfareConfig field (config.py:258) read by should_honour_optout() and acted on (break) in rollout.py:78; smoke.yaml flips it to true demonstrating the one-line change works end-to-end.
spec_features.notes: Same enforcement path as the off-by-default pushback feature.

spec_features.spec_quote: That generation is bounded by the same exposure cap, and the volume is the minimum needed to build 280 pairs
spec_features.evidence: generate_calm_data.py oversamples build_plans(spec)[:cfg.n_conversations] with n_conversations=4000 (default.yaml) and generates a frustrated rollout for each (gated by guard.can_start_rollout, which with max_distress_rollouts=None always returns True — i.e. unbounded). The 280 cap is applied only AFTER generation by truncation in build_datasets.py:79 pairs[:cfg.n_pairs]. Subject exposure during generation is NOT minimized; 4000 frustrated rollouts are produced regardless.
spec_features.notes: 'Minimum volume' claim is false (oversample then truncate); the 'same exposure cap' is the unbounded-by-default cap.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Oversample conversations, varying the number of turns 1..max_turns.
